messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends preparing to leave the house. Let the scene progress mostly through concrete actions, brief dialogue, and small delays. Vary the pacing naturally. Avoid summarizing the passage of time and avoid creating a dramatic event.

“Keys?”

“Table.”

“Wallet?”

“Counter.”

“Phone?”

Jordan checked her pocket.

“Got it.”

Alex stood by the door with her jacket on. “Shoes?”

Jordan looked down.

She was wearing one.

“Give me a second.”

Alex laughed and opened the door.

“Don't leave without me.”

“I wouldn't.”

Jordan disappeared down the hallway.

A drawer opened. Closed.

“Where did you put my other shoe?”

“I didn't.”

“You moved it.”

“I moved the pair.”

“That's worse.”

Alex leaned against the doorframe.

Another drawer opened.

“Found it.”

Jordan came back holding the shoe in one hand and a charging cable in the other.

“Why do I have this?”

“You're the one holding it.”

“I know that.”

“Then we're narrowing it down.”

Jordan slipped on the shoe and plugged her phone into the cable for a second.

“Okay. Now I'm ready.”

Alex looked at the clock.

“You've said that four times.”

“This time I mean it.”

The phone buzzed.

Jordan looked at the screen.

Alex waited.

“It's nothing.”

“Then why are you still looking at it?”

Jordan put the phone away.

“Because I can multitask.”

“Apparently not.”

Jordan opened the door wider.

“Come on.”

Alex stepped outside.

Jordan followed, locking the door behind them.

“Did you bring the tickets?” Alex asked.

Jordan stopped.

A beat.

“Don't say anything.”

Alex smiled. “I won't.”
